sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Moers sets its parking fees by ordinance, and the ordinance is changed for budget and tax reasons as much as for traffic ones. The council amended the Parkgebührenordnung on 3 July 2024, in force from 15 July 2024: 1.00 euro per 30 minutes in the Neumarkt zone, 0.50 euro per 20 minutes in Zone 1, and a day, week and month ticket for the two largest lots, Mühlenstraße and Friedrich-Ebert-Platz [5]. The city announced that those two areas would charge 4 euros a day, 10 euros a week and 30 euros a month from 15 July 2024, after a political motion and a majority council decision to secure the municipal budget [6]. The question was already open in 2022, when the planning committee had not yet decided on higher fees and the city expected to owe 19 percent VAT on most of its managed car parks [2].

That VAT question is the reason for the next change. On 24 September 2026 the planning committee adopted new fees because of a legal requirement to charge VAT on stand-alone municipal car parks; the city says the aim is not to raise revenue. The new tariffs are stated to apply from 1 January 2027, for example 1.20 euros per 30 minutes in tariff A and 4.50 euros a day in tariff D, and the free 20 minutes stay [12]. We found no source on whether the full council must also confirm them. Under the current rules, fees apply Monday to Friday 9 to 19 and Saturday 9 to 16, and Sundays and public holidays are free; the city says about 5,300 spaces are available in the centre and that this is sufficient overall [13]. Resident parking has existed since 1995, with nine zones and a permit of 30 euros a year, according to the city's information sheet [9]. The city's 2018 transport plan listed a garage at Kautzstraße and underground garages at Königlicher Hof and Neuer Wall as items to be examined, not decisions [0].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main change in the centre is the loss of one garage. ENNI closed the Parkhaus Kautzstraße, in service since 1972, in June 2023 because strengthening work was needed for structural safety and was not technically feasible [3]. In November 2023 the planning committee asked for three variants of a replacement to be worked out further [4]. In an announcement of 19 September 2024, ENNI said demolition would start on 9 October and be finished by 22 November 2024 [3]. In March 2025 Radio K.W. reported that demolition alone had cost almost 100,000 euros against an original estimate of 80,000 euros for demolition and the new lot together, and that the interim lot with 61 spaces was expected to cost 215,000 euros [10]. Since 1 July 2026 about 60 surface spaces have been in use on the site at tariff B; ENNI says a new garage is to follow in the long term, while Radio K.W. reported that about 280 central spaces were lost, that timing and design are open and that the cheapest of three variants was once estimated at 8 million euros [11]. A further garage, in a housing project called Moerser Benden West, is only a perspective project in the city's 2024 overview, meant to replace spaces that would be lost on the Mühlenstraße lot [8].

The Parkleitsystem was put back into operation on 15 November 2022 after the data capture on some lots had to be converted [1]; the city now says it connects 9 public car parks and 2 private garages [15]. ENNI said in September 2024 that public charging points in the city would double to 50 by the end of 2024 and reach about 190 by 2030 [7].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
ENNI manages the public parking on behalf of the city; the council sets the tariffs and the revenue goes to the city budget [14]. ENNI lists twelve public car parks in the centre with more than 2,500 spaces: five barrier-controlled with 678 spaces and seven pay-and-display with 1,835 spaces, the largest being Mühlenstraße with 1,000 spaces [14]. We found no private-garage operators or tariffs in readable sources.

Our Moers data cover five lots from the city's own live feed, with 1,463 spaces: Mühlenstraße (699), Friedrich-Ebert-Platz (299), Braun (215), Bankstraße (140) and Kastell (110). The feed's capacity for Mühlenstraße is lower than ENNI's 1,000. Occupancy from late September to mid-October 2026 averaged about 20% on weekdays and 13% at weekends, weighted by spaces, so the centre has a great deal of spare room. The exception is the Kastell lot, which averaged 53% and reached 95% on a Sunday afternoon; it was full for about 18% of the hours measured. The Braun lot is the only one that is busier at weekends than on weekdays (32% against 18%) and reached 98% on a Saturday. The large lots on Mühlenstraße and Friedrich-Ebert-Platz, which are the ones priced at 4 euros a day, averaged 17% and 11%. These are about three weeks of data, and the summer holidays had just ended.
